rationale: This qualitative study (40 key informant interviews and focus group discussions across six iTaukei villages in Fiji, analyzed thematically) examines village-level water committees—a formal requirement to access support under the Water Authority of Fiji Rural Water Scheme—focusing on committee membership rules, user/gender participation, and polycentric coordination across household, committee, village, and district/provincial levels (primary mechanism: participation_assistance). The central empirical outcomes analyzed across the four results themes are institutional and governance intermediate outcomes (committee structures, reporting and accountability mechanisms, village/committee decision-making processes, gendered member roles, and proactive vs. reactive maintenance routines), placing the primary outcome in administrative_outcome.
